page: Microsoft Azure E64-16ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for workloads requiring an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU allocation. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance runs an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. It is provisioned with 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core, backed by 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. The platform includes hardware vector acceleration such as AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The primary architectural distinction of this instance is its memory subsystem, supplying 512.0 GB of RAM, or 32.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmark evaluations reflect this emphasis, where the PassMark memory score reached 2827.67, positioning it in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is measured at 103.1 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 59.48 GB/sec for write operations. Multi-core compute performance sits within the middle 50 percent, delivering a Geekbench multi-core score of 10172.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 15535.97, consistent with an 8-core physical allocation.

Storage provisions include 2577 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity alongside premium storage capability, providing fast ephemeral storage without requiring external attachments for intermediate data. The system does not incorporate any GPU hardware accelerators. For networking and addressing, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E64-16ds_v5 delivers high resource density for scenarios where memory capacity is the governing constraint rather than raw compute scaling. The combination of 512 GB of RAM and 2.5 TB of local fast storage provides an efficient footprint for large in-memory databases such as Redis, enterprise database engines, in-memory caching layers, and high-footprint ETL pipeline processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-16ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. Operating on x86_64 architecture with 48 MB L3 cache, the instance delivers a substantial 512.0 GB of system memory, equating to 32.0 GB per vCPU. Bundled with 2577 GB of local SSD ephemeral storage, the hardware includes support for AVX-512 and hardware-accelerated cryptography, though it lacks dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark performance highlights strong memory capability, with PassMark memory testing reaching 2827.67, ranking in the top 25 percent, while CPU metrics remain balanced in the middle tier. With 15.93 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 103.1 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth, the configuration provides an efficient profile for memory-constrained workloads including large in-memory caching tiers, enterprise relational databases, big data analytics, and memory-intensive ETL transformations.
